Stage 6B complete. Implementation report:

## 0. Housekeeping: rename done first

`corpus/ledger.py` → `corpus/session_index.py` (`SessionIndex`, `SessionIndexError`, `session_ordinal`, stage `session_index`, script constants/paths, `session-index.public.json`, tests, and F1 prereg/AGENTS prose). Behaviour preserved — full suite green throughout; the persisted schema string stays byte-frozen by design. `Context Ledger` now unambiguously means the Stage 6 mechanism. Left intentionally untouched: frozen reports, campaign-exclusion wording, synthetic planted strings, session-memory files.

## 1. Architecture

`LedgerState + ActivationRequest + ActivationPolicy → ActivationResult` via pure `activate()`. New sibling package `src/project_context/activation/` (`model.py`, `engine.py`); 6A core diff-free.

## 2. Layers preserved

Eligibility gate (terminal → per-status code; contradicted verification; repo-mismatch as world boundary) runs before relevance; relevance never resurrects ineligible items. Blocked obligations stay eligible — readiness is a relevance question, answered per request.

## 3. Request

New versioned `ActivationRequest` (repo/paths/components/task/operation/evidence_refs, all optional, exact structural overlap only). Compiler's `ContextRequest` deliberately not reused — budget/admission fields would invite the miniature-compiler failure; 6C bridges them.

## 4. Decisions

`ACTIVE/DORMANT/INELIGIBLE/UNKNOWN` + sorted reason codes, matched scope/deps, consulted features, epistemic marker (assumptions/pending keep their status, never promoted), policy id. Repo equality alone never activates; unresolved ≠ relevant; UNKNOWN never defaults to ACTIVE. Output is item-id order, not a ranking. No scores, no representation choice.

## 5. Relationships

Only `depends_on` propagates: one snapshot pass, ACTIVE-only, non-propagating (boundedness test-pinned with a 3-chain). Supersession/contradiction handled by the gate; other types are lineage.

## 6. Policy & baselines

`activation-policy-v1` (typed) plus naive modes in the same engine: `all_unresolved`, `scope_only` (no validity gate — activates superseded items), `newest` (top-3, request ignored).

## 7. Fixtures & oracle

10 authored core cases (all §12 scenarios A–J, 19 requests) + 8 seeded held-out cases (disjoint vocabulary, independent oracle in `generate.py`, `--check` byte-stable). Truth is tests/eval-only; runtime files carry no oracle tokens (pinned).

## 8. Results (offline)

Typed: **precision 1.0, recall 1.0, 0 false/missed over 87 decisions** incl. exact reason codes; 12 UNKNOWN, all oracle-matching abstentions. Baselines: all_unresolved P 0.32 (48 false, 5 leaks); scope_only 13 false, 8 leaks, 7 stale, 2 superseded; newest 47 false. Dimensions separate, no composite score.

## 9. CLI

`ledger activate <case> --request-file … [--mode]` and `ledger eval-activations activation-v1` (SYNTHETIC-labelled; truth never in normal output).

## 10. Tests & docs

33 new tests covering all 21 required properties; 6A digest pinned (`cce87221…`); import-direction pins both ways; compiler/OpenCode presence pins. **409 passed** (376 rename baseline + 33), `ruff` clean. Docs: `experiments/activation-v1/` (spec, policy, generator), architecture + README sections, `docs/stage-6b-report.md`.

## 11. Deviations & environment notes

`ledger_ordinal`→`session_ordinal` and stage-string renames went slightly beyond the suggested module rename, contained and test-covered. Two parallel owner commits landed mid-session (`2d53c97` committed my 6A work; F1 work continued alongside) — no overlaps, final validation on the merged tree. One pre-existing ruff sort error fixed en passant.

## 12. Stop

6C not started. The open question stands as framed: how an activated item becomes an ordinary `ContextCandidate` with no durable-state privilege.

Stage 6B is **exactly the result we wanted**. The strongest part is not the 1.0/1.0 score; it is that the architecture now cleanly distinguishes:

```text
persisted
→ eligible
→ relevant now
→ candidate
→ admitted
```

and **UNKNOWN remains a legitimate abstention rather than silently becoming ACTIVE**. That is a very important property.

I would treat the 1.0 precision/recall over 87 synthetic decisions as **mechanism validation on the controlled fixture family**, not as evidence that activation is solved in real work. The held-out cases help show the rules are not merely hardcoded to the authored examples, but Stage 6B still establishes a structural result, not ecological or behavioural utility.

The next step should indeed be **Stage 6C — the Compiler Adapter**. And I would make this stage deliberately small. If 6C starts inventing priorities, relevance scores, special budget rules, or presentation formats, it will undermine the architecture we've carefully built.

The question for 6C should be:

> **Can activated durable state be represented as ordinary compiler candidates while preserving its provenance and epistemic meaning, without gaining any admission privilege because it came from the Ledger?**

Here is the prompt I would give the local agent.

Implement **Stage 6C — Ledger-to-Compiler Candidate Adapter** in `project-context`.

Stages 6A and 6B are complete.

The current architecture is:

```text
LedgerEvent[]
    ↓
LedgerState
    ↓
ActivationRequest
    ↓
activate()
    ↓
ActivationResult
```

Stage 6B established a deterministic distinction between:

```text
ACTIVE
DORMANT
INELIGIBLE
UNKNOWN
```

Stage 6C introduces one narrow bridge:

```text
ACTIVE ledger state
        ↓
adapter
        ↓
ordinary ContextCandidate[]
```

The key requirement is:

> **Durable state receives no special admission privilege merely because it came from the Context Ledger.**

The existing Context Compiler remains sovereign over what enters the finite context window.

---

# 0. Inspect repository reality first

Before modifying anything:

Read:

```text
AGENTS.md
README.md
specs/architecture.md
docs/stage-6a-report.md
docs/stage-6b-report.md
experiments/designs/F4B-stateful-context-ledger.md
experiments/designs/F10-compiler-integration.md
```

Inspect the actual implementations of:

```text
src/project_context/ledger/
src/project_context/activation/
src/project_context/compiler/
src/project_context/domain/
```

and especially determine the real schema and semantics of:

```text
ContextCandidate
ContextRequest
ContextItem
compiler eligibility metadata
representation/fidelity fields
authority
scope
freshness
provenance
identity
token/budget fields
```

Also inspect:

* compiler fixture conventions;
* compiler determinism guarantees;
* compiler compatibility tests;
* evidence/provenance conventions;
* existing adapters between domain representations.

Do not force this prompt's names or shapes over better repository abstractions.

Run the full baseline suite before implementation.

---

# 1. Stage 6C question

The exact question is:

> Can an ACTIVE ledger item be translated into a normal compiler candidate while retaining the information necessary for later governance, representation, tracing and evaluation?

Stage 6C is an **adapter test**, not a behavioural experiment.

It must establish only that the architectural boundary works.

It does not establish that:

```text
Ledger state improves model performance
activation improves behaviour
the compiler should admit ledger items
the chosen representation is optimal
automatic extraction works
live injection helps
```

---

# 2. Architecture

The target boundary is:

```text
LedgerState
    +
ActivationResult
        ↓
LedgerCandidateAdapter
        ↓
ContextCandidate[]
        ↓
EXISTING Context Compiler
```

Stage 6C should stop after proving that the resulting candidates can flow through the existing compiler normally.

Do not implement runtime injection.

Do not modify OpenCode.

Do not implement Stage 6D.

---

# 3. Fundamental invariant: no durable-state privilege

This is the most important Stage 6C rule.

An activated ledger item must not automatically become:

```text
PIN
highest priority
zero-cost
mandatory
always eligible
always selected
freshest
highest authority
```

merely because its source is the Ledger.

The adapter may preserve facts such as:

```text
authority = user
scope = parser
verification = unverified
lifecycle = active
source = context_ledger
```

but the compiler must treat those properties through its ordinary policies.

For example:

```text
user-authored constraint
```

may legitimately receive strong standing because its **authority is user-derived**.

That is different from:

```text
source == ledger
```

receiving strong standing.

Add tests specifically proving this distinction.

---

# 4. Input boundary

Prefer the adapter to consume explicit Stage 6B output rather than recomputing activation.

Conceptually:

```python
adapt(
    state: LedgerState,
    activation: ActivationResult,
    ...
) -> tuple[ContextCandidate, ...]
```

or the closest repository-native form.

Stage 6C must not:

```text
re-run activation
infer relevance
reinterpret dormant state
resurrect UNKNOWN items
inspect unrelated ledger items
```

Only items that Stage 6B marked ACTIVE are eligible for candidate creation.

The following produce no ordinary candidate:

```text
DORMANT
INELIGIBLE
UNKNOWN
```

If the repository needs an audit receipt for non-candidate decisions, keep that separate from `ContextCandidate[]`.

---

# 5. Preserve epistemic state

This is critical.

An ACTIVE item may still be:

```text
assumption
pending verification
unverified
derived
contradicted evidence pair
```

Activation means:

> this matters now.

It does not mean:

> this is established truth.

The adapter must preserve sufficient metadata so a downstream representation or governance layer can distinguish:

```text
Schema v2 is canonical.
    verified/project decision
```

from:

```text
The provider probably returns null here.
    unverified assumption
```

and:

```text
The race fix appears complete.
    pending verification
```

Do not flatten all three into equivalent plain text.

If `ContextCandidate` already supports suitable metadata, use it.

If it does not, make the smallest compatible extension justified by this requirement.

Do not redesign the whole compiler domain model.

---

# 6. Preserve authority by origin

Map ledger authority into existing compiler authority semantics cleanly.

Stage 6A currently preserves origins conceptually such as:

```text
system
user
project
tool
agent
derived
```

Inspect the compiler's actual authority vocabulary.

Create an explicit mapping.

Requirements:

```text
user-derived ledger state
    retains user-derived authority

project-derived state
    retains project standing

tool observation
    remains evidence/data rather than instruction

agent-authored claim
    does not become user/project authority

derived state
    remains derived
```

Unknown mappings must fail clearly or remain explicitly unknown.

Never silently promote authority during adaptation.

---

# 7. Preserve scope

Activation already uses scope to decide present relevance.

That does not mean scope can be discarded afterwards.

The compiler and later debugger should still be able to know:

```text
repository
component
path
task/session scope
```

where those exist.

Preserve existing scope metadata in the candidate.

Do not infer missing scope.

Do not convert missing scope into global scope.

---

# 8. Preserve lifecycle provenance without making it compiler policy

An active candidate should retain traceability back to:

```text
ledger item
activation decision
source provenance
events that established current state
relationships relevant to activation
```

But avoid putting an entire event history into the compiler candidate.

Prefer references/identities/digests where possible.

Conceptually:

```text
candidate
    source_type = ledger
    source_item_id = ...
    activation_policy = ...
    activation_reasons = ...
    provenance_ref = ...
```

Use repository conventions rather than these exact fields.

The compiler needs enough lineage to explain later:

> Why was this information available for admission?

It does not need the whole ledger event stream.

---

# 9. Identity

Candidate identity must be deterministic under identical input.

Inspect existing candidate-ID/content-ID rules.

The adapter should make it possible to distinguish:

```text
same ledger item
same projected state
same activation
```

from:

```text
same semantic item after its state changed
```

Do not invent IDs from mutable timestamps if content-derived identity is the existing convention.

Do not expose private statement content in externally published identifiers if repository privacy conventions prohibit that.

Add determinism tests.

---

# 10. Candidate content

Use the smallest truthful content representation needed by the existing compiler.

Do not implement the final reader-facing rendering.

For example, if the compiler expects a candidate payload, it may be acceptable to supply the ledger item's current canonical statement plus structured metadata.

Do not yet decide among:

```text
warning block
table
compact record
prose summary
full event history
reference
```

Those are representation questions.

Stage 6C needs a **canonical candidate payload**, not a polished final prompt representation.

The adapter must not use an LLM to rewrite ledger state.

---

# 11. Representation boundary

Preserve this distinction:

```text
ledger item
    structured durable state

activated ledger item
    relevant structured state

ContextCandidate
    information available for compiler consideration

rendered context
    later representation selected for model consumption
```

Stage 6C stops at the third line.

If `ContextCandidate` requires a representation field today, use the least transformative existing representation and mark it accordingly.

Do not add a ledger-specific rendering system.

---

# 12. Token/cost handling

Do not give ledger candidates a fictional zero token cost.

Use existing compiler conventions for candidate cost estimation.

If exact rendered token cost is not knowable until later representation/rendering:

```text
UNKNOWN
```

or an existing estimated-cost state is preferable to fake precision.

Do not use ledger statement character length as though it were exact provider token cost unless that is already an explicit compiler approximation.

---

# 13. Freshness and verification

Do not recompute Stage 6A/6B state inside the adapter.

The adapter should preserve current projected properties.

Example:

```text
decision v1
status = superseded
```

will never arrive because 6B marks it ineligible.

But an ACTIVE result such as:

```text
pending verification
```

must retain that pending state.

No adapter code should silently convert:

```text
active + unverified
```

into:

```text
active + verified
```

---

# 14. Dependencies and relationships

Do not flatten the entire ledger graph into candidate text.

Preserve only relationship information needed downstream.

For example:

```text
depends_on
verification lineage
source relation
```

may deserve candidate metadata or provenance references.

Relationships already consumed solely for activation need not automatically be copied if no later component needs them.

Document the decision.

Avoid candidate objects containing arbitrary graph snapshots.

---

# 15. Adapter receipt / trace

Provide a deterministic trace of adaptation.

Something conceptually like:

```text
LedgerAdapterReceipt

activation_item_id
activation_state
candidate_id or none
mapped_authority
mapped_scope
epistemic_state
source_provenance
reason
```

This may be useful for F10 and the debugger later.

Do not mix this receipt into the candidate if the repository already separates decisions from artifacts.

The important question is that later we can answer:

```text
Which ledger item produced this candidate?
Why was it allowed to reach the compiler?
Which metadata was preserved?
```

---

# 16. Compiler compatibility experiment

Build a deterministic Stage 6C fixture/test.

The test is NOT:

> Does the ledger candidate win?

The test is:

> Does it compete normally?

Construct cases where activated ledger candidates compete with ordinary non-ledger candidates.

At minimum include:

### Case A — ledger item should be admitted

The ledger candidate contains genuinely useful eligible information and fits normally.

### Case B — ordinary candidate should beat ledger candidate

The ledger item is active/relevant but a stronger or more useful ordinary candidate should be selected instead under the existing compiler policy.

This proves no ledger privilege.

### Case C — ledger candidate excluded by budget

An active ledger item is a valid candidate but the compiler legitimately leaves it out.

This must be allowed.

### Case D — authority derives from source, not ledger

Compare:

```text
user-derived ledger constraint
agent-derived ledger statement
```

Ensure their compiler standing differs because of authority metadata, not because both are Ledger items.

### Case E — unverified state survives candidate creation

An active assumption or pending-verification item reaches the compiler marked as such.

### Case F — multiple ledger candidates

Several activated items become ordinary candidates.

The adapter must not rank them.

### Case G — mixed source pool

Compiler receives candidates from:

```text
ledger
file/retrieval/other existing sources
```

and processes them under normal policy.

---

# 17. Byte-/behaviour-compatibility

This is extremely important.

Existing compiler behaviour **without ledger candidates** should remain unchanged.

Where the repository currently guarantees byte-identical traces or deterministic output, preserve that guarantee.

Add a regression test:

```text
existing compiler input
without Stage 6C candidate source
        ↓
exact same compiler result/trace
```

Do not introduce new default fields that alter old hashes/traces unless absolutely necessary.

If a domain-schema extension is required, design compatibility carefully and document it.

---

# 18. No candidate-source shortcut

Search the compiler after implementation and ensure nothing equivalent exists:

```python
if candidate.source == "ledger":
    priority += 100
```

or:

```python
if candidate.from_ledger:
    eligible = True
```

or:

```python
ledger_candidates = pinned + others
```

Add an architectural/property test where feasible.

---

# 19. Do not modify activation semantics

Stage 6B is complete.

Do not tune activation rules in Stage 6C because a candidate behaves poorly in a compiler test.

If a genuine 6B defect is discovered:

1. record it;
2. add a minimal failing 6B test;
3. fix it separately;
4. rerun the frozen 6B evaluation;
5. report the deviation.

Do not silently adjust activation to help 6C results.

---

# 20. Synthetic evaluation

Create a Stage 6C design or preregistration before treating any compatibility result as evidence.

Question:

> Can activated ledger state enter the existing Context Compiler as ordinary candidates while preserving authority, scope, provenance and epistemic state, without receiving ledger-specific admission privilege?

Measurements should be structural:

```text
candidate conversion success
metadata preservation
identity determinism
lineage preservation
ordinary-compiler compatibility
ledger privilege violations
legacy compiler compatibility
```

Do not report model accuracy.

No model calls are needed.

---

# 21. CLI / debugging surface

Only add CLI support if it materially improves inspection.

A useful flow might be conceptually:

```text
contextlab ledger candidates <case> --request-file ...
```

showing:

```text
ACTIVE LEDGER ITEMS
...
```

755: def _depends_on_id(candidate_id: str, live: list[ContextCandidate]) -> bool:

input.content:
"""Adapt ACTIVE ledger items into ordinary compiler candidates.

Mapping (every choice documented; nothing here is a relevance judgement):

- input: one `LedgerState`, one `ActivationResult`, one adapter policy id.
  Only ACTIVE decisions yield candidates. Activation is consumed, never
  recomputed: dormant, ineligible and unknown items yield receipts with
  `candidate_id = None`.
- `candidate_id = ledger-<item_id>-<digest12>`, where the digest covers
  item id, lifecycle status, verification, statement digest, activation
  policy id and sorted reason codes. Identical input reproduces it;
  any meaningful state change alters it. No statement content enters
  the identifier (privacy: live statements may be private).
- `content_identity = ledger-item-<item_id>`: one semantic item, so
  alternative-form exclusion can never merge two ledger items.
- `content`: the canonical statement verbatim, except that unverified
  epistemic state the render pipeline would otherwise flatten is kept
  visible with a deterministic status tag (`[Unverified assumption]`,
  `[Pending verification]`). The render joins contents only, so this
  tag is what preserves "matters now" without claiming "established
  truth". No LLM rewriting, no polished rendering.
- `kind`: the ledger item kind (obligation, assumption, ...). The
  engine reads kind only for render decoration, so this preserves
  meaning with zero admission effect.
- `source_kind = "ledger"`, `source_ref = <item_id>`: lineage, not
  privilege. Standing never keys off these fields (pinned by tests).
- `requirement`: PREFERRED for user/system/project authority,
  DISCRETIONARY otherwise. Authority-derived standing, exactly as
  ordinary pools treat user instructions versus tool evidence. Never
  MANDATORY/REQUIRED: adapted state must earn admission and must be
  allowed to lose or be omitted by budget.
- `relevance`: one fixed adapter default for every adapted candidate.
  No per-item scoring, hence no adapter ranking; ties break by
  candidate_id in the engine, neutrally.
- `order_role`: instruction for constraints/decisions, task for
  obligations, state for unresolved failures, evidence for the rest.
  Render order only.
- eligibility flags: True with reasons recording the preserved facts
  (scope dimensions, verification state, authority origin). The adapter
  is the pool-builder for ledger items, as fixtures are for ordinary
  ones; activation already applied the validity gate for this
  computation. Adapting output for any other computation is a harness
  error, documented here.
- `token_count`: the repository's existing word-based approximation
  over the final content, `token_source = "approximation"`. No fake
  precision, no zero costs.
- single canonical form: `representation_id = "ledger-full"`,
  `form_rank = 3`, `min_rank = 0`, `is_default_form = True`.
- `depends_on`: ledger dependencies remapped to co-adapted candidate
  ids; dependencies outside the ACTIVE batch are omitted and named in
  the receipt (activation-time facts, not compiler graph snapshots).
- `coverage_keys`, `group_id`: empty/None. Adapted candidates earn
  admission through the ordinary earn rule.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from project_context.activation.model import ActivationResult, ActivationState
from project_context.compiler.domain import ContextCandidate, RequirementClass
from project_context.domain.items import estimate_tokens
from project_context.ledger.projection import LedgerState, ProjectedItem
from project_context.ledger.records import Authority, ItemKind

ADAPTER_POLICY_ID = "ledger-adapter-v1"
ADAPTER_RECEIPT_SCHEMA = "project_context.ledger_adapter_receipt.v1"
ADAPTER_RELEVANCE = 0.5

_PREFERRED_AUTHORITIES = frozenset({Authority.USER, Authority.SYSTEM, Authority.PROJECT})

_ORDER_ROLE = {
    ItemKind.CONSTRAINT: "instruction",
    ItemKind.DECISION: "instruction",
    ItemKind.OBLIGATION: "task",
    ItemKind.UNRESOLVED_FAILURE: "state",
    ItemKind.ASSUMPTION: "evidence",
    ItemKind.PENDING_VERIFICATION: "evidence",
    ItemKind.RESULT: "evidence",
    ItemKind.DEPENDENCY: "evidence",
}

_EPISTEMIC_TAG = {
    ItemKind.ASSUMPTION: "[Unverified assumption]",
    ItemKind.PENDING_VERIFICATION: "[Pending verification]",
}

_AUTHORITY_REASON = {
    Authority.USER: "user-derived directive standing",
    Authority.SYSTEM: "system standing",
    Authority.PROJECT: "project standing",
    Authority.TOOL: "tool evidence: data, never directive",
    Authority.AGENT: "agent-authored: data, never user/project authority",
    Authority.DERIVED: "derived state",
}


def _candidate_digest(item: ProjectedItem, reason_codes: tuple[str, ...], policy_id: str) -> str:
    basis = "|".join(
        [
            item.item.item_id,
            item.status.value,
            item.verification.value,
            item.statement_digest,
            policy_id,
            ",".join(reason_codes),
        ]
    )
    return hashlib.sha256(basis.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


def _content(item: ProjectedItem, epistemic: str | None) -> str:
    statement = item.item.statement
    if epistemic == "unverified":
        tag = _EPISTEMIC_TAG.get(item.item.kind)
        if tag is not None:
            return f"{tag} {statement}"
    return statement


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LedgerAdapterReceipt:
    """Deterministic trace of one adaptation decision: which ledger item,
    whether it became a candidate, what metadata was preserved, and why."""

    item_id: str
    activation_state: str
    candidate_id: str | None
    mapped_authority: str
    mapped_requirement: str | None
    epistemic: str | None
    scope: dict[str, Any]
    dropped_dependencies: tuple[str, ...]
    reason: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "schema_version": ADAPTER_RECEIPT_SCHEMA,
            "item_id": self.item_id,
            "activation_state": self.activation_state,
            "candidate_id": self.candidate_id,
            "mapped_authority": self.mapped_authority,
            "mapped_requirement": self.mapped_requirement,
            "epistemic": self.epistemic,
            "scope": dict(self.scope),
            "dropped_dependencies": list(self.dropped_dependencies),
            "reason": self.reason,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "LedgerAdapterReceipt":
        version = data.get("schema_version", ADAPTER_RECEIPT_SCHEMA)
        if version != ADAPTER_RECEIPT_SCHEMA:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported LedgerAdapterReceipt schema: {version!r}")
        return cls(
            item_id=data["item_id"],
            activation_state=data["activation_state"],
            candidate_id=data.get("candidate_id"),
            mapped_authority=data["mapped_authority"],
            mapped_requirement=data.get("mapped_requirement"),
            epistemic=data.get("epistemic"),
            scope=dict(data.get("scope", {})),
            dropped_dependencies=tuple(data.get("dropped_dependencies", [])),
            reason=data.get("reason", ""),
        )


def adapt(
    state: LedgerState,
    activation: ActivationResult,
    *,
    policy_id: str = ADAPTER_POLICY_ID,
) -> tuple[tuple[ContextCandidate, ...], tuple[LedgerAdapterReceipt, ...]]:
    """Adapt every ACTIVE decision into an ordinary candidate plus a
    receipt per decision. Deterministic; sorted by item id."""
    by_item = {entry.item.item_id: entry for entry in state.items}
    active_ids = {
        d.item_id for d in activation.decisions if d.state is ActivationState.ACTIVE
    }
    # Candidate ids first, so depends_on can remap within the batch.
    planned: dict[str, str] = {}
    for decision in sorted(activation.decisions, key=lambda d: d.item_id):
        if decision.item_id not in active_ids or decision.item_id not in by_item:
            continue
        entry = by_item[decision.item_id]
        digest = _candidate_digest(entry, tuple(sorted(decision.reason_codes)), policy_id)
        planned[decision.item_id] = f"ledger-{decision.item_id}-{digest}"

    candidates: list[ContextCandidate] = []
    receipts: list[LedgerAdapterReceipt] = []
    for decision in sorted(activation.decisions, key=lambda d: d.item_id):
        entry = by_item.get(decision.item_id)
        if entry is None or decision.state is not ActivationState.ACTIVE:
            receipts.append(
                LedgerAdapterReceipt(
                    item_id=decision.item_id,
                    activation_state=decision.state.value,
                    candidate_id=None,
                    mapped_authority=entry.item.authority.value if entry else "unknown",
                    mapped_requirement=None,
                    epistemic=None,
                    scope=entry.item.scope.to_dict() if entry else {},
                    dropped_dependencies=(),
                    reason="not active: no candidate produced",
                )
            )
            continue
        candidate_id = planned[decision.item_id]
        preferred = entry.item.authority in _PREFERRED_AUTHORITIES
        requirement = RequirementClass.PREFERRED if preferred else RequirementClass.DISCRETIONARY
        content = _content(entry, decision.epistemic)
        token_count, token_source = estimate_tokens(content)
        depends_on = tuple(
            sorted(planned[dep] for dep in entry.depends_on if dep in planned)
        )
        dropped = tuple(sorted(dep for dep in entry.depends_on if dep not in planned))
        scope = entry.item.scope
        scope_bits = []
        if scope.repo is not None:
            scope_bits.append(f"repo={scope.repo}")
        if scope.component is not None:
            scope_bits.append(f"component={scope.component}")
        if scope.paths:
            scope_bits.append(f"paths={','.join(scope.paths)}")
        if scope.task is not None:
            scope_bits.append(f"task={scope.task}")
        candidates.append(
            ContextCandidate(
                candidate_id=candidate_id,
                content_identity=f"ledger-item-{entry.item.item_id}",
                representation_id="ledger-full",
                form_rank=3,
                min_rank=0,
                source_kind="ledger",
                source_ref=entry.item.item_id,
                kind=entry.item.kind.value,
                content=content,
                token_count=token_count,
                token_source=token_source,
                requirement=requirement,
                order_role=_ORDER_ROLE[entry.item.kind],
                scope_eligible=True,
                scope_reason=(
                    "activation-established scope: " + (";".join(scope_bits) or "unscoped")
                ),
                freshness_eligible=True,
                freshness_reason=(
                    f"ledger verification={entry.verification.value}; "
                    "epistemic state preserved, not promoted"
                ),
                authority_eligible=True,
                authority_reason=_AUTHORITY_REASON[entry.item.authority],
                depends_on=depends_on,
                group_id=None,
                group_required=False,
                coverage_keys=(),
                relevance=ADAPTER_RELEVANCE,
                is_default_form=True,
            )
        )
        receipts.append(
            LedgerAdapterReceipt(
                item_id=decision.item_id,
                activation_state=decision.state.value,
                candidate_id=candidate_id,
                mapped_authority=entry.item.authority.value,
                mapped_requirement=requirement.value,
                epistemic=decision.epistemic,
                scope=scope.to_dict(),
                dropped_dependencies=dropped,
                reason=";".join(sorted(decision.reason_codes)),
            )
        )
    return tuple(candidates), tuple(receipts)


def adapt_case(
    state: LedgerState,
    activation: ActivationResult,
    ordinary: list[ContextCandidate],
    *,
    policy_id: str = ADAPTER_POLICY_ID,
) -> tuple[tuple[ContextCandidate, ...], tuple[LedgerAdapterReceipt, ...]]:
    """Adapted ledger candidates plus an ordinary pool, sorted by
    candidate id. The adapter never reorders by importance."""
    adapted, receipts = adapt(state, activation, policy_id=policy_id)
    pool = tuple(sorted([*ordinary, *adapted], key=lambda c: c.candidate_id))
    return pool, receipts

input.content:
# adapter-v1 — ledger-to-compiler candidate compatibility experiment

SYNTHETIC. NO MODEL CALLS. NOT A BOOK RESULT UNTIL EXPLICITLY PROMOTED.

## Question

Can activated ledger state enter the existing Context Compiler as
ordinary candidates while preserving authority, scope, provenance and
epistemic state, without receiving ledger-specific admission privilege?

## Non-claims

No model behaviour is measured here. A successful result establishes
only that the architectural boundary works: adapted candidates compete
normally. It says nothing about ledger utility, activation ecology,
optimal representation, extraction, or injection.

## Hypotheses (until the run)

- H1: every ACTIVE fixture item converts to exactly one candidate with
  preserved metadata; non-ACTIVE items convert to none.
- H2: adapted candidates admit, lose, or are omitted by budget under
  the unchanged compiler policy across the seven compatibility cases.
- H3: standing differences between adapted candidates derive from
  authority metadata, never from ledger source.

## Falsification

If any adapted candidate is MANDATORY/REQUIRED, ranked by the adapter,
or admitted over budget; if compiler sources branch on ledger origin;
if legacy fixtures change output — the boundary has failed and the
report must say so.

## Layout

```text
experiments/adapter-v1/
  README.md                 this file
  spec.yaml                 frozen contract (see specs/experiment-contract.md)
```

Fixtures live under `fixtures/adapter-v1/` (committed JSON is
canonical). No generator: seven hand-built adversarial cases.

## Reproduce

```text
contextlab ledger candidates <case> --request-file <activation-request> --compile
pytest tests/test_adapter.py
```

# Frozen experiment contract: adapter-v1. See specs/experiment-contract.md.
question: >-
  Can ACTIVE ledger state be translated into ordinary compiler
  candidates while retaining authority, scope, provenance and epistemic
  meaning, without gaining admission privilege from ledger origin?
hypotheses: [H1-faithful-conversion, H2-normal-competition, H3-authority-not-source]
population: fixtures/adapter-v1 manifest v1 (7 synthetic compatibility
  cases reusing activation-v1 streams)
independent_variable: candidate pool composition (adapted ledger plus
  ordinary candidates per case)
controlled_variables:
  - ledger state per case (frozen events.jsonl, projected deterministically)
  - activation per case (frozen request JSON, typed policy)
  - ordinary pool per case (frozen candidates JSON)
  - compiler request per case (frozen compile JSON, required_ids empty)
  - policy: compiler-policy-v1 (unchanged)
  - token counting: fixture-declared counts for ordinary candidates,
    word-approximation for adapted candidates (labelled)
  - no models, no network, no retrieval, no injection
conditions: [adapted-plus-ordinary compiled under the existing staged engine]
measurements:
  - candidate conversion success (ACTIVE to exactly one candidate)
  - metadata preservation (authority band, scope, epistemic tag,
    provenance, identity determinism)
  - lineage preservation (adapter receipts per decision)
  - ordinary-compiler compatibility (admit / lose / omit per oracle)
  - ledger privilege violations (mandatory bands, per-item relevance,
    source branches in compiler, budget overruns)
  - legacy compiler compatibility (existing fixtures byte-identical)
success_criteria:
  - every case compiles per its oracle with no privilege violation
  - no adapted candidate MANDATORY/REQUIRED or distinctly relevant
  - compiler sources contain no ledger/activation branch
failure_criteria:
  - any oracle mismatch on the seven cases
  - any privilege violation
  - any legacy fixture output change
  - nondeterministic rerun output
  - any oracle truth token in runtime sources or fixture runtime files
falsification:
  - an adapted candidate that cannot lose (always admitted regardless
    of pool and budget)
  - standing that follows source_kind rather than authority metadata
seed_strategy: none required (no randomness anywhere in the pipeline)
provider_model: synthetic, no model calls
cost_ceiling: zero spend (offline suite)

# Stage 6C report — Ledger-to-Compiler Candidate Adapter

## Purpose

Bridge one narrow gap: ACTIVE ledger state becomes ordinary compiler
candidates for the unchanged Context Compiler. Stage 6C demonstrates
that the boundary works — faithful conversion, normal competition, no
privilege. It does not demonstrate utility, optimal representation, or
anything behavioural.

Design: `experiments/adapter-v1/` (frozen compatibility contract,
question, conditions, measurements, falsification). No behavioural run
is attached; nothing here is book evidence.

## Architecture

```text
Stage 6A:  events → LedgerState
Stage 6B:  LedgerState + ActivationRequest → ActivationResult
Stage 6C:  ActivationResult → ContextCandidate[] → EXISTING compiler
Stage 6D:  (future) selected bundle → explicit runtime injection
```

Dependency direction: ledger → activation → ledger_adapter →
compiler domain interface. The compiler never imports upward (pinned).

## Adapter mapping

`adapt(state, activation)` consumes Stage 6B output without
recomputing it. Only ACTIVE decisions yield candidates; everything
else yields a receipt with no candidate. Per ACTIVE item:
`candidate_id = ledger-<item>-<digest12>` over id, status,
verification, statement digest, policy id and sorted reasons
(deterministic; state changes alter it); `content_identity =
ledger-item-<item>`; content is the verbatim statement except
unverified assumptions/pending claims keep a deterministic status tag
(`[Unverified assumption]`, `[Pending verification]`), because the
render joins contents only and would otherwise flatten them into fact;
`kind` is the ledger kind (decoration only, zero admission effect);
`source_kind = "ledger"`, `source_ref = item id` (lineage, never
standing); requirement PREFERRED for user/system/project authority,
DISCRETIONARY otherwise (authority-derived, mirroring ordinary pools;
never MANDATORY/REQUIRED); one fixed relevance for all adapted
candidates (no adapter ranking; engine tie-breaks by id); order roles
instruction/task/state/evidence by kind (render order only);
eligibility flags True with reasons recording scope, verification and
authority facts; single canonical form (full, floor 0); token counts
from the existing word approximation, labelled as such; `depends_on`
remapped to co-adapted candidate ids, outsiders named in the receipt;
no coverage keys, no groups. `adapt_case` merges with an ordinary pool
sorted by candidate id.

## Authority mapping

user → PREFERRED ("user-derived directive standing"); system/project
→ PREFERRED; tool → DISCRETIONARY ("data, never directive"); agent →
DISCRETIONARY ("never user/project authority"); derived →
DISCRETIONARY. Unknown authorities cannot occur (closed enum); any
future addition maps explicitly or fails at the mapping table, never
silently promotes.

## Scope, epistemic, lifecycle, identity, provenance

Scope dimensions preserved in reasons and receipts, never inferred,
never defaulted to global. Epistemic state preserved three ways:
kind, freshness reason, and render-visible tag; verified items carry
no tag. Lifecycle enters identity (status/verification in the digest)
and eligibility (only ACTIVE arrives). Provenance is
source_kind/source_ref plus per-decision receipts answering which item
produced which candidate, why it was allowed through, and what was
kept. Full event history is deliberately not copied.

## Compiler compatibility cases

Seven synthetic cases (required_ids always empty, so everything is
earned): ledger items admitted (A); stronger ordinary candidate wins
the budget (B); valid items omitted by budget with success preserved
(C); user outranks agent by authority metadata (D); pending claim
renders marked (E); three ledger candidates convert unranked (F);
mixed pool with full trace coverage (G).

## Legacy compatibility

Existing compiler fixtures produce byte-identical results; the staged
engine, policy, and domain records are untouched. No new candidate
field was added, so no hash/trace changed.

## Tests

`tests/test_adapter.py`, 29 tests: conversion cardinality,
no-recomputation, authority/epistemic/scope/provenance preservation,
receipt round-trips, identity determinism and state sensitivity,
no-ranking, dependency remap, no mandatory bands, lose-by-policy,
omit-by-budget, source-swap trace identity (relabelled source_kind
changes no decision), compiler source scans, all seven oracle cases,
mixed-pool trace coverage, legacy determinism, forbidden imports,
one-way import direction, 6A digest and 6B oracle re-verified,
runtime-file truth separation, OpenCode absence, CLI behaviour.

Results: 409 passing at baseline; **438 passing** at finish (29 new),
`ruff check .` clean. No historical artifacts modified; no run outputs
fabricated; no behavioural run executed. No 6B defect was found; no
activation semantics were touched.

## Invariants

Activation is not admission (compiler decides); ledger provenance
never grants privilege (behavioural + scan pins); compiler sources
branch on no origin (pinned); adapter ranks nothing (pinned);
budgets bind adapted candidates like all others.

## What Stage 6C demonstrates

Activated durable state can be presented to the existing compiler as
ordinary context candidates while retaining its important metadata
and without bypassing ordinary compiler decisions.

## What it does NOT demonstrate

Ledger utility, admission correctness, activation ecology, optimal
representation, injection safety/usefulness, extraction.

## Deferred work

Stage 6D (explicit intervention-capable runtime rendering and
injecting a compiler-selected bundle; observer stays read-only;
invocations captured for evaluation) is next and explicitly not
started. F10 is untouched.

No adapted candidate above DISCRETIONARY--or-PREFERRED; ledger items demonstrably lose (B) and are omitted (C); relabelling `source_kind` leaves the trace byte-identical; compiler sources contain no ledger/activation branch (scan-pinned); legacy fixtures byte-identical (no domain change was needed).

## Tests

29 new tests covering all 28 required properties: conversion cardinality, no-recomputation, authority mapping (incl. no user-authority for agent state, project standing), tool-evidence stays evidence, epistemic survival through render, scope/provenance/receipts, identity determinism + state sensitivity, no ranking, dependency remap, privilege behaviour (lose/omit/swap), all seven oracles, mixed-pool validation, legacy determinism, forbidden imports, one-way imports, 6A digest + 6B oracle re-verified, truth separation, OpenCode absence, CLI.

## Validation

**438 passed** (409 baseline + 29), `ruff check .` clean. No historical artifacts modified, no runs fabricated, no behavioural work. No 6B defect found; activation untouched.

## What 6C demonstrates / does not

Demonstrates: activated durable state can enter the existing compiler as ordinary candidates with metadata intact and without bypassing compiler decisions. Does not demonstrate: utility, admission correctness, activation ecology, optimal representation, injection safety, extraction.

## Deviations

None structural. Two test-side fixes during development (pool filter, trace-identity assertion direction); budgets tuned empirically to exact-fit values (C:108, D:14) and frozen in `compile.json`.

Stopped before 6D as instructed — no injection, no OpenCode changes, no F10 alteration.

Stage 6C is strong. The most important result is that the Ledger has now crossed into the existing compiler **without contaminating it**: no upward import, no `source_kind=="ledger"` shortcut, no mandatory band, no ranking in the adapter, and the same compiler can legitimately reject an activated ledger candidate.

One thing I would record explicitly before moving on: the **exact-fit budgets in cases C and D are fixture mechanics, not evidence about realistic budgets**. They are perfectly acceptable for proving “can lose” and “can be omitted,” but later experiments should not inherit 108 or 14 as meaningful thresholds.

We are now at the first stage where I would become substantially more conservative, because **6D crosses from observation/decision machinery into intervention**.

The next question should not yet be “does the runtime improve coding?” It should be:

> **Can we render and inject an already-selected compiler bundle into a model request, through a separate intervention-capable integration, while keeping the existing observer read-only and making the resulting request independently observable?**

That gives us a closed experimental loop without yet claiming usefulness.

Implement **Stage 6D — Explicit Context Runtime Injection** in `project-context`.

Stages 6A–6C are complete.

The current architecture is:

```text
deterministic renderer
```

with the resulting invocation independently observable by the existing capture system.

The key architectural rule is:

> **The observer remains an observer. Intervention happens through a separate integration.**

Do not modify the existing read-only OpenCode capture integration into a mutating plugin.

Before changing anything:

Read and obey:

* `AGENTS.md`
* `README.md`
* `specs/architecture.md`
* `docs/stage-6a-report.md`
* `docs/stage-6b-report.md`
* `docs/stage-6c-report.md`

Inspect:

* existing compiler bundle/output types;
* existing renderer(s), if any;
* OpenCode V2 observer integration;
* capture schemas;
* request/invocation identity;
* privacy/export rules;
* current test harnesses;
* any existing mock OpenCode or request interception mechanism.

Run the full baseline suite first.

The repository is authoritative.

---

# 1. Stage 6D question

The exact Stage 6D question is:

> Can a compiler-selected bundle be rendered and injected into a model request through an explicitly intervention-capable runtime while preserving provenance, leaving the observer read-only, and allowing us to verify exactly what the model received?

This is an **integration/mechanism test**.

It is not yet a behavioural effectiveness experiment.

Stage 6D does NOT establish:

* that injected state improves task success;
* that activation is ecologically correct;
* that the selected bundle is optimal;
* that the Ledger is useful;
* that automatic extraction works;
* that the full Context Runtime should be deployed.

---

# 2. Separate integration

Create a separate intervention surface.

Conceptually:

```text
integrations/
    opencode/             existing observer, unchanged/read-only

    opencode-runtime/     new explicit intervention integration
```

Adapt naming to repository conventions.

The existing observer must remain structurally independent and read-only.

Add architecture/import tests proving this.

Do not share mutable hooks between them merely for convenience.

---

# 3. Runtime architecture

Target something conceptually equivalent to:

```text
ContextRequest
    ↓
Ledger projection
    ↓
Activation
    ↓
Ledger adapter
    ↓
candidate pool
    ↓
Context Compiler
    ↓
selected bundle
    ↓
Renderer
    ↓
Runtime Injection Receipt
    ↓
OpenCode request mutation
    ↓
model invocation
    ↓
existing Observer captures actual request
```

The important distinction is:

```text
intended injection
    ≠
observed final request
```

The system should record both.

This gives us a way to detect integration drift.

---

# 4. Renderer first, injector second

Keep rendering separate from mutation.

Prefer a pure function conceptually like:

```python
render_bundle(bundle, render_policy) -> RenderedContext
```

Then:

```python
inject(request, rendered_context) -> InjectionResult
```

Do not combine selection, rendering and hook mutation into one opaque function.

This separation is critical for testing.

---

# 5. Deterministic rendering

Stage 6D needs one canonical representation sufficient for integration testing.

Do NOT start a broad representation optimisation experiment.

The renderer should:

* be deterministic;
* preserve item boundaries;
* preserve epistemic labels where required;
* preserve authority-sensitive wording where required;
* preserve selected ordering;
* contain no hidden/unselected items;
* contain no event history unless explicitly selected;
* avoid an LLM rewrite;
* avoid semantic compression.

If existing compiler output already contains a canonical rendering mechanism, reuse it.

Do not invent a second rendering architecture unnecessarily.

---

# 6. Epistemic truth must survive rendering

This is non-negotiable.

These must remain distinguishable to the downstream model:

```text
verified result
unverified assumption
pending verification
constraint
decision
unresolved failure
```

For example, this is unacceptable:

```text
The race condition is fixed.
```

if the Ledger actually says:

```text
pending_verification
```

The rendered form must communicate something equivalent to:

```text
[PENDING VERIFICATION]
The race condition appears fixed but has not been verified.
```

Use repository terminology.

Do not turn metadata into false factual certainty.

---

# 7. Preserve provenance without dumping metadata

The model-facing rendering does not need commit IDs, digests, event IDs or internal run codes.

Preserve meaningful provenance conceptually:

```text
user requirement
project decision
tool observation
agent assumption
verification result
```

Machine-level provenance remains in receipts/traces.

This follows the book-wide rule:

> provenance is rigorous underneath, cognitively light above.

---

# 8. Injection must be explicit

Do not create ambient automatic mutation.

The intervention runtime should require an explicit mode/configuration.

Conceptually:

```text
observer mode
    no mutation

runtime mode
    explicit intervention enabled
```

A fresh/default installation must not unexpectedly begin rewriting model context.

Make the opt-in visible in CLI/config/test setup.

---

# 9. No observer mutation

The current OpenCode observer must remain unable to:

* add messages;
* change system prompts;
* remove content;
* alter tool definitions;
* rewrite request bodies;
* suppress messages;
* change model selection.

Pin this with tests.

If the observer needs awareness that an injection occurred, it should learn that by **observing the resulting request**, not by becoming part of the mutating pathway.

---

# 10. Injection receipt

Every intervention should emit a deterministic receipt.

Conceptually:

```text
InjectionReceipt

runtime_request_id
compiler_bundle_id
rendered_context_digest
candidate_ids
render_policy_id
injection_location
pre_injection_request_digest
post_injection_request_digest
injected_bytes
status
failure_reason
```

Use repository-native identities.

Do not include private raw content in published receipts where privacy rules prohibit it.

The receipt should let us answer:

> What did the runtime intend to add?

---

# 11. Observation reconciliation

This is the most important Stage 6D mechanism.

After injection, the existing observer should capture the actual request.

Create a deterministic reconciliation step:

```text
InjectionReceipt
    +
ObservedInvocation
        ↓
ReconciliationResult
```

Questions:

```text
Was the intended rendered block present?

Was it byte-identical where expected?

Was its order preserved?

Was anything duplicated?

Was anything dropped?

Did another layer alter it?

Did the final request contain unexpected material?
```

The observer remains independently read-only.

The reconciliation proves whether the intervention actually reached the model boundary as intended.

---

# 12. Three identities

Keep these distinct:

```text
selected bundle identity

rendered context identity

observed final request identity
```

Do not assume equality.

This distinction will matter later for caching, provider wrappers and runtime transformations.

---

# 13. Injection location

Pick one explicit, documented injection position for Stage 6D.

For example, if OpenCode supports a dedicated system/context block, use the least invasive stable location.

Do not test multiple placements yet unless repository reality requires it.

Record:

```text
injection_location
```

in the receipt.

Placement experiments belong later.

---

# 14. Collision handling

Define deterministic behaviour if the target request already contains a prior runtime block.

Do not blindly append duplicate runtime state.

Possible policy:

```text
no runtime block
    → insert

same runtime block / same digest
    → idempotent, no duplicate

different runtime block
    → fail loudly or explicit replacement mode
```

Choose based on OpenCode hook semantics.

Do not silently stack repeated runtime payloads.

Add idempotence tests.

---

# 15. Failure should fail safe

If rendering or injection cannot be proven correct:

Prefer:

```text
no intervention
+
explicit failure receipt
```

over partially mutating context.

Do not leave a half-written context block.

Failure modes should be typed.

Potential examples:

```text
render_failed
unsupported_request_shape
injection_conflict
duplicate_runtime_block
observer_reconciliation_failed
request_identity_mismatch
```

Use existing error conventions.

---

# 16. Synthetic harness first

Do not begin with a real coding session.

Build a completely synthetic request harness.

It should exercise:

```text
ordinary request
+
compiler-selected synthetic bundle
+
runtime rendering
+
runtime injection
+
observer capture
+
reconciliation
```

No model call required initially.

Prove the complete loop structurally.

---

# 17. Required synthetic cases

At minimum include:

### A. No selected candidates

Runtime makes no mutation.

Observer sees original request.

### B. One selected ordinary candidate

Candidate renders once and appears exactly where intended.

### C. Selected Ledger candidate

Epistemic/provenance representation survives.

### D. Mixed selected bundle

Ordinary + Ledger candidates render in compiler-selected order.

### E. Candidate rejected by compiler

Never appears in rendered/injected context.

### F. Repeated runtime invocation

No duplicate block.

### G. Conflicting pre-existing runtime block

Fails according to declared policy.

### H. Observer reconciliation mismatch

Deliberately corrupt synthetic post-injection request and prove reconciliation detects it.

### I. UNKNOWN/DORMANT ledger state

Never reaches runtime because it never became a candidate/selected item.

### J. Privacy trap

Synthetic private-looking material not selected by compiler must never appear merely because it existed upstream.

---

# 18. No bypass around compiler

Stage 6D must consume the compiler's selected bundle.

It must not independently add:

```text
active ledger items
important constraints
verification warnings
```

outside that bundle.

Search for and prohibit shortcuts conceptually like:

```python
render(selected_bundle)
+ render(all_active_constraints)
```

If a constraint belongs in context, it must have been admitted through the normal candidate/compiler path.

This preserves:

```text
Persistence is not activation.
Activation is not admission.
Admission is not injection unless explicitly rendered.
```

---

# 19. Existing compiler remains sovereign

Do not change compiler policy to make Stage 6D demonstrations convenient.

If a fixture needs a selected item:

construct the fixture/pool/budget so normal compiler policy selects it.

Do not pin Ledger candidates.

Do not raise bands.

Do not add runtime-required candidate IDs.

---

# 20. Runtime block markers

If the injected context needs delimiters, use a stable deterministic wrapper.

Conceptually:

```text
[CONTEXT RUNTIME]

...selected rendered context...

[/CONTEXT RUNTIME]
```

Use better repository-native naming if appropriate.

Markers should support:

* detection;
* idempotence;
* reconciliation.

Do not include run IDs or commit hashes in model-facing text.

---

# 21. Model-facing text

Apply the reader-first principle here too.

The model should receive concise semantic context, not infrastructure archaeology.

Good:

```text
[CONSTRAINT]
Do not modify migration 017.

[PENDING VERIFICATION]
The race-condition fix has not yet passed verification.
```

Bad:

```text
ledger-item-341
activation-policy-v1
run-72
event-882
digest-abcd...
```

Machine metadata belongs in receipts.

---

# 22. CLI

Add a deliberate inspection command if useful.

Conceptually:

```text
contextlab runtime render ...
contextlab runtime inject --synthetic ...
contextlab runtime reconcile ...
```

or one coherent command following existing CLI conventions.

Avoid CLI proliferation.

A useful synthetic demonstration could show:

```text
SELECTED CANDIDATES
...

RENDERED BLOCK
...

INJECTION
success

OBSERVATION
matched

RECONCILIATION
PASS
```

Label synthetic runs clearly.

---

# 23. No live model calls yet

Stage 6D does not require a model.

Do not spend model tokens.

Do not start a live behavioural experiment.

The structural integration loop can and should be earned first.

---

# 24. Optional single throwaway integration probe

Only after the synthetic harness passes, you may prepare—but do not automatically run—a minimal throwaway OpenCode integration probe if needed to confirm hook shape.

If actual OpenCode behaviour cannot be validated without one real request, stop and report that requirement rather than silently starting a live study.

Do not count such a probe as evidence.

---

# 25. Stage 6D measurements

Use structural measurements only:

```text
render determinism

selected-item coverage
    selected items represented / selected items expected

unselected leakage
    unselected items appearing in runtime block

duplication count

order preservation

epistemic-label preservation

authority/provenance preservation

injection success

observer reconciliation success

idempotence

legacy observer compatibility
```

No composite score.

---

# 26. Tests

At minimum verify:

1. renderer deterministic;
2. zero candidates yields zero mutation;
3. selected candidate rendered exactly once;
4. unselected candidate never rendered;
5. Ledger candidate gets no runtime privilege;
6. mixed-source selected bundle preserves compiler order;
7. epistemic labels survive rendering;
8. authority provenance survives where model-facing semantics require it;
9. machine metadata stays out of model-facing block;
10. receipt contains lineage;
11. request before/after digests differ only when injection occurs;
12. repeated identical injection is idempotent;
13. conflicting runtime block handled explicitly;
14. partial injection cannot occur;
15. observer integration remains read-only;
16. runtime integration alone owns mutation;
17. synthetic observer captures post-injection request;
18. reconciliation passes on correct request;
19. reconciliation fails on tampered request;
20. unselected private/trap content cannot leak;
21. DORMANT/UNKNOWN state cannot bypass earlier stages;
22. compiler source remains free of runtime/ledger branches;
23. 6A digest remains stable;
24. 6B evaluation remains stable;
25. 6C compatibility fixtures remain stable;
26. legacy compiler tests unchanged;
27. legacy observer tests unchanged;
28. runtime package has no model-provider dependency unless strictly required for OpenCode hook types;
29. hidden oracle truth never enters rendering;
30. full suite passes.

Extend architecture/import-direction tests.

---

# 27. Experiment/design record

Create a Stage 6D design document before describing the result as evidence.

Question:

> Can the output of the existing Context Compiler be injected through a separate explicit runtime and independently observed at the model-request boundary without bypassing compiler policy or modifying the observer?

This is an integration result.

It does not test behavioural utility.

---

# 28. Documentation

Update architecture to:

```text
Stage 6A
events
→ LedgerState

Stage 6B
LedgerState + request
→ activation

Stage 6C
activation
→ ordinary ContextCandidate[]

Existing Compiler
candidates
→ selected bundle

Stage 6D
selected bundle
→ deterministic render
→ explicit runtime injection

Existing Observer
actual invocation
→ capture

Reconciliation
intended injection
↔ observed invocation
```

Highlight:

> The component that changes context is not the component that measures context.

That separation should remain permanent.

---

# 29. Stage report

Create:

```text
docs/stage-6d-report.md
```

Report:

* renderer;
* intervention integration;
* injection location;
* opt-in mechanism;
* receipts;
* reconciliation;
* synthetic fixtures;
* idempotence;
* failure handling;
* privacy behaviour;
* observer compatibility;
* tests;
* architectural invariants;
* what Stage 6D establishes;
* what it does not establish.

---

# 30. Stop point

Do NOT begin Stage 6E automatic extraction.

Do NOT begin F4B behavioural evaluation.

Do NOT modify F10.

Do NOT run a real ecological campaign through the intervention runtime.

Do NOT turn the runtime on for ordinary work.

Stop after the synthetic injection/reconciliation mechanism is complete and validated.

Return the full Stage 6D report.

The next major decision should then be whether to:

```text
A. test automatic state extraction (Stage 6E)
```

or:

```text
B. keep state oracle/manual and run the first behavioural F4B experiment
```

We should make that choice based on the completed 6D architecture rather than assuming automatic extraction belongs next.

## I would **not automatically do 6E next**

This is important.

Once 6D works, we will finally have:

```text
oracle/manual state
→ Ledger
→ activation
→ normal candidate
→ compiler
→ injection
→ independently observed request
```

At that point, we can test the **actual central hypothesis** without introducing another noisy component:

> Is selectively maintaining and reconstructing durable state better than carrying history or injecting all unresolved state?

That is F4B.

My inclination is that **F4B should probably come before automatic extraction**. Otherwise, if the eventual result fails, we'd have too many possible explanations:

```text
bad extraction?
bad ledger?
bad activation?
bad admission?
bad rendering?
bad model behaviour?
```

With manual/oracle state, we isolate the runtime mechanism first.

So after 6D returns, I would seriously consider **jumping directly to F4B with oracle-authored state**, and only build 6E if the runtime itself earns its place.

"""Explicit context runtime injection (Stage 6D): render, inject, reconcile.

Boundary (pinned by tests):

- the runtime consumes only compiler-selected bundles, never ledger or
  activation state directly (no bypass around the compiler);
- rendering is pure and deterministic; injection is explicit and
  opt-in; observation stays with the existing read-only observer;
- intended injection and observed invocation are recorded separately
  and reconciled deterministically;
- no model calls, no network, no wall-clock reads, no randomness;
- the runtime never imports ledger, activation, providers, readers,
  behaviour, evaluation, or the OpenCode integration.
"""

from project_context.runtime.inject import RUNTIME_MODE, inject
from project_context.runtime.model import (
    INJECTION_LOCATION,
    InjectionReceipt,
    ReconciliationResult,
    RenderedBlock,
    RenderPolicy,
    RuntimeError,
)
from project_context.runtime.reconcile import reconcile
from project_context.runtime.render import render_bundle

__all__ = [
    "INJECTION_LOCATION",
    "RUNTIME_MODE",
    "InjectionReceipt",
    "ReconciliationResult",
    "RenderPolicy",
    "RenderedBlock",
    "RuntimeError",
    "inject",
    "reconcile",
    "render_bundle",
]

"""Runtime records: render policy, rendered block, receipts, reconciliation.

All records are frozen dataclasses with schema versions and JSON
round-trips. Receipts carry digests, counts, and identities — never raw
model-facing content (privacy: live statements may be private; receipts
are the shareable artifact, rendered blocks are local-only).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

RENDER_POLICY_SCHEMA = "project_context.runtime_render_policy.v1"
RENDERED_BLOCK_SCHEMA = "project_context.rendered_block.v1"
INJECTION_RECEIPT_SCHEMA = "project_context.injection_receipt.v1"
RECONCILIATION_SCHEMA = "project_context.reconciliation_result.v1"

BLOCK_OPEN = "[CONTEXT RUNTIME]"
BLOCK_CLOSE = "[/CONTEXT RUNTIME]"
INJECTION_LOCATION = "system-append"

RENDER_POLICY_ID = "runtime-render-v1"


class RuntimeError(Exception):
    """Typed runtime failure with a machine-readable code."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str):
        super().__init__(f"{code}: {detail}")
        self.code = code
        self.detail = detail


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RenderPolicy:
    """How a selected bundle becomes model-facing text. One canonical
    policy in Stage 6D; placement experiments belong later."""

    policy_id: str = RENDER_POLICY_ID
    policy_version: str = "1"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "schema_version": RENDER_POLICY_SCHEMA,
            "policy_id": self.policy_id,
            "policy_version": self.policy_version,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "RenderPolicy":
        version = data.get("schema_version", RENDER_POLICY_SCHEMA)
        if version != RENDER_POLICY_SCHEMA:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported RenderPolicy schema: {version!r}")
        return cls(
            policy_id=data.get("policy_id", RENDER_POLICY_ID),
            policy_version=data.get("policy_version", "1"),
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RenderedBlock:
    """Deterministic model-facing text for one selected bundle, plus its
    identity. Empty selections render to empty text with item_count 0;
    the injector refuses those (no mutation for nothing)."""

    bundle_id: str
    policy_id: str
    text: str
    item_count: int
    digest: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "schema_version": RENDERED_BLOCK_SCHEMA,
            "bundle_id": self.bundle_id,
            "policy_id": self.policy_id,
            "text": self.text,
            "item_count": self.item_count,
            "digest": self.digest,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "RenderedBlock":
        version = data.get("schema_version", RENDERED_BLOCK_SCHEMA)
        if version != RENDERED_BLOCK_SCHEMA:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported RenderedBlock schema: {version!r}")
        return cls(
            bundle_id=data["bundle_id"],
            policy_id=data.get("policy_id", RENDER_POLICY_ID),
            text=data["text"],
            item_count=int(data["item_count"]),
            digest=data["digest"],
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InjectionReceipt:
    """What the runtime intended and what it did. `pre_digest` and
    `post_digest` use the same identity basis as the observer-side
    integrity hash, so reconciliation can prove byte-equality."""

    runtime_request_id: str
    bundle_id: str
    rendered_digest: str
    candidate_ids: tuple[str, ...]
    render_policy_id: str
    injection_location: str
    pre_digest: str
    post_digest: str
    injected_bytes: int
    status: str
    failure_reason: str | None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "schema_version": INJECTION_RECEIPT_SCHEMA,
            "runtime_request_id": self.runtime_request_id,
            "bundle_id": self.bundle_id,
            "rendered_digest": self.rendered_digest,
            "candidate_ids": list(self.candidate_ids),
            "render_policy_id": self.render_policy_id,
            "injection_location": self.injection_location,
            "pre_digest": self.pre_digest,
            "post_digest": self.post_digest,
            "injected_bytes": self.injected_bytes,
            "status": self.status,
            "failure_reason": self.failure_reason,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "InjectionReceipt":
        version = data.get("schema_version", INJECTION_RECEIPT_SCHEMA)
        if version != INJECTION_RECEIPT_SCHEMA:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported InjectionReceipt schema: {version!r}")
        return cls(
            runtime_request_id=data["runtime_request_id"],
            bundle_id=data["bundle_id"],
            rendered_digest=data["rendered_digest"],
            candidate_ids=tuple(data.get("candidate_ids", [])),
            render_policy_id=data.get("render_policy_id", RENDER_POLICY_ID),
            injection_location=data.get("injection_location", INJECTION_LOCATION),
            pre_digest=data["pre_digest"],
            post_digest=data["post_digest"],
            injected_bytes=int(data["injected_bytes"]),
            status=data["status"],
            failure_reason=data.get("failure_reason"),
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReconciliationResult:
    """Intended injection versus observed invocation. PASS requires every
    check; anything else is FAIL with per-check evidence. Checks skipped
    for non-injected receipts report `not_applicable` as their status."""

    runtime_request_id: str
    status: str
    checks: dict[str, Any]
    duplication_count: int
    detail: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "schema_version": RECONCILIATION_SCHEMA,
            "runtime_request_id": self.runtime_request_id,
            "status": self.status,
            "checks": dict(self.checks),
            "duplication_count": self.duplication_count,
            "detail": self.detail,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "ReconciliationResult":
        version = data.get("schema_version", RECONCILIATION_SCHEMA)
        if version != RECONCILIATION_SCHEMA:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported ReconciliationResult schema: {version!r}")
        return cls(
            runtime_request_id=data["runtime_request_id"],
            status=data["status"],
            checks=dict(data.get("checks", {})),
            duplication_count=int(data.get("duplication_count", 0)),
            detail=data.get("detail", ""),
        )

"""Explicit injection into a synthetic OpenCode-shaped request.

The request dict mirrors the V2 bridge record shape (system/messages/
tools/options). Injection appends one marked text block to the END of
the system array: the least invasive stable location, leaving every
existing block untouched and ordered.

Fail-closed contract:

- `mode` must be the literal runtime mode; anything else raises
  `opt_in_required`. A default/fresh setup can never mutate.
- malformed requests raise `unsupported_request_shape` (programmer
  error, never a receipt).
- a differing pre-existing runtime block yields a failure receipt with
  NO mutation (`injection_conflict`).
- an identical pre-existing block yields an idempotent no-op receipt.
- an empty rendered block yields an empty no-op receipt.
- partial writes never occur: the new system array is built first and
  swapped once.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
from typing import Any

from project_context.opencode.bridge import integrity_of
from project_context.runtime.model import (
    BLOCK_CLOSE,
    BLOCK_OPEN,
    INJECTION_LOCATION,
    InjectionReceipt,
    RenderedBlock,
    RuntimeError,
)

RUNTIME_MODE = "runtime"
OBSERVER_MODE = "observe"


def _system_texts(request: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    return [
        block["text"]
        for block in request["system"]
        if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("text"), str)
    ]


def inject(
    request: dict[str, Any],
    rendered: RenderedBlock,
    *,
    request_id: str,
    mode: str,
    candidate_ids: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], InjectionReceipt]:
    """Inject the rendered block, or refuse with an explicit receipt."""
    if mode != RUNTIME_MODE:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "opt_in_required",
            f"injection requires mode={RUNTIME_MODE!r}; got {mode!r}",
        )
    if (
        not isinstance(request, dict)
        or not isinstance(request.get("system"), list)
        or not isinstance(request.get("messages"), list)
        or not isinstance(request.get("tools"), dict)
        or not isinstance(request.get("options"), dict)
    ):
        raise RuntimeError("unsupported_request_shape", "request is not a V2-shaped record")
    pre_digest = integrity_of(request)
    base_receipt = {
        "runtime_request_id": request_id,
        "bundle_id": rendered.bundle_id,
        "rendered_digest": rendered.digest,
        "candidate_ids": tuple(candidate_ids),
        "render_policy_id": rendered.policy_id,
        "injection_location": INJECTION_LOCATION,
        "pre_digest": pre_digest,
    }
    if not rendered.text or rendered.item_count == 0:
        copied = copy.deepcopy(request)
        return copied, InjectionReceipt(
            **base_receipt,
            post_digest=pre_digest,
            injected_bytes=0,
            status="noop_empty",
            failure_reason=None,
        )
    existing = [text for text in _system_texts(request) if BLOCK_OPEN in text]
    if existing:
        if any(text == rendered.text for text in existing):
            copied = copy.deepcopy(request)
            return copied, InjectionReceipt(
                **base_receipt,
                post_digest=pre_digest,
                injected_bytes=0,
                status="noop_idempotent",
                failure_reason=None,
            )
        copied = copy.deepcopy(request)
        return copied, InjectionReceipt(
            **base_receipt,
            post_digest=pre_digest,
            injected_bytes=0,
            status="failed",
            failure_reason="injection_conflict",
        )
    mutated = copy.deepcopy(request)
    mutated["system"] = [*mutated["system"], {"type": "text", "text": rendered.text}]
    post_digest = integrity_of(mutated)
    _ = BLOCK_CLOSE
    return mutated, InjectionReceipt(
        **base_receipt,
        post_digest=post_digest,
        injected_bytes=len(rendered.text.encode("utf-8")),
        status="injected",
        failure_reason=None,
    )

"""Reconciliation: intended injection versus observed invocation.

Compares the injection receipt plus the rendered reference against the
record the existing observer captured. Every check is structural and
byte-exact where it matters:

- record_valid: the observed record passes bridge validation;
- markers_present: a runtime block marker survived to observation;
- block_exact: an occurrence equals the intended text byte for byte;
- block_once: exactly one exact occurrence (duplication count kept);
- order_preserved: the exact block is the last system block (the
  append location) and internal section order matches the reference;
- integrity_match: observer-side integrity equals the receipt's
  post_digest — byte-equality of the whole request, catching any
  added, dropped, or altered material anywhere.

Non-injected receipts reconcile differently: noop_empty requires the
markers ABSENT and integrity equal to pre (nothing added, nothing
changed); noop_idempotent requires the block present once with
integrity equal to post; failed receipts are not_applicable (the
failure receipt itself is the record).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from project_context.opencode.bridge import integrity_of, validate_record
from project_context.runtime.model import BLOCK_OPEN, InjectionReceipt, ReconciliationResult, RenderedBlock


def _system_texts(observed: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    system = observed.get("system")
    if not isinstance(system, list):
        return []
    return [
        block["text"]
        for block in system
        if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("text"), str)
    ]


def _section_bodies(text: str) -> list[str]:
    lines = text.split("\n")
    bodies: list[str] = []
    current: list[str] = []
    for line in lines[1:]:
        if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]") and current is not None and bodies is not False:
            pass
        current.append(line)
    _ = current
    # Sections are header line + body lines separated by blank lines.
    chunks = [chunk for chunk in "\n".join(lines[1:-1]).split("\n\n") if chunk.strip()]
    for chunk in chunks:
        parts = chunk.split("\n", 1)
        bodies.append(parts[1] if len(parts) == 2 else parts[0])
    return bodies


def reconcile(
    receipt: InjectionReceipt, rendered: RenderedBlock, observed: dict[str, Any]
) -> ReconciliationResult:
    """Reconcile one injection against one observed record. Pure."""
    texts = _system_texts(observed)
    markers = sum(1 for text in texts if BLOCK_OPEN in text)
    occurrences = sum(1 for text in texts if text == rendered.text)
    record_ok = not validate_record(observed)
    integrity_ok = bool(texts) and integrity_of(observed) == (
        receipt.post_digest if receipt.status != "noop_empty" else receipt.pre_digest
    )

    if receipt.status == "failed":
        return ReconciliationResult(
            runtime_request_id=receipt.runtime_request_id,
            status="not_applicable",
            checks={"reason": "no injection was attempted"},
            duplication_count=occurrences,
            detail="failure receipt stands alone; nothing to reconcile",
        )
    if receipt.status == "noop_empty":
        passed = record_ok and markers == 0 and integrity_ok
        return ReconciliationResult(
            runtime_request_id=receipt.runtime_request_id,
            status="pass" if passed else "fail",
            checks={
                "record_valid": record_ok,
                "markers_absent": markers == 0,
                "integrity_match": integrity_ok,
            },
            duplication_count=occurrences,
            detail="empty render must leave the request untouched",
        )
    last_is_block = bool(texts) and texts[-1] == rendered.text
    order_ok = last_is_block and _section_bodies(texts[-1]) == _section_bodies(rendered.text)
    checks = {
        "record_valid": record_ok,
        "markers_present": markers >= 1,

def _section_bodies(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Item body sequence inside a rendered block, in order. Headers
    (marker lines and [KIND] lines) are skipped; bodies determine order."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    inner = lines[1:-1] if len(lines) >= 2 else []
    chunks = [chunk for chunk in "\n".join(inner).split("\n\n") if chunk.strip()]
    bodies = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        parts = chunk.split("\n", 1)
        bodies.append(parts[1] if len(parts) == 2 else parts[0])
    return bodies
